Patient presents with {Pathology: severe bilateral pes planovalgus / hypotonia / hypotonia / subtalar joint instability / pronation with dynamic arch collapse / dynamic calcaneal valgus/ bilateral equinovarus alignment}. PHYSICAL ASSESSMENT & BIOMECHANICS:
* Subtalar & Midtarsal Alignment: {Subtalar Alignment: Severe calcaneal eversion reducible to neutral / Calcaneal inversion-forefoot supination and cavus arch/ Calcaneal valgus with forefoot abduction / Rigid pes valgus / Significant midfoot sag}.

Observational gait analysis demonstrates {Gait Deviations: excessive pronation and arch flattening at midstance / excessive supination and varus heel angle at stance/ lack of stable base of support / dynamic valgus thrust / out-toeing with medial heel whip / delayed push-off}. {+ Toe walking: Pt. also displays difficulty with heel toe gait pattern and remains plantarflexed (toe walks) during stance to toe off.}

shoe-lift.text:
Patient was seen at the North/South office for evaluation, fitting, and delivery of a Left/Right heel lift to support healing and offload posterior compartment structures.

Clinical Rationale & Indication:
Patient presents secondary to {Indication: Post-Operative Achilles Tendon Repair / Acute Achilles Tendon Rupture (Non-Surgical Protocol) / Insertional Achilles Tendinitis / Midportion Achilles Tendinopathy / Achilles Paratenonitis / Retrocalcaneal Bursitis}. The heel lift is medically necessary to place the ankle in controlled plantarflexion, relax tension on the gastrocnemius-soleus complex, protect the healing tendon repair from sudden passive stretch, reduce inflammatory strain, and facilitate pain-free weight-bearing ambulation.

Objective Assessment & Device Placement:
Device Fit: Fit with a {Lift Thickness: ⅛" (3mm) / ¼" (6mm) / ⅜" (9mm) / ½" (12mm) / ⅝" (15mm) / ¾" (18mm) / [Custom Thickness]} {Lift Placement: firm cork-leather heel lift / multi-layer stackable Achilles wedge / viscoelastic silicone heel cushion / full-sole tapered shoe modification} placed in Left/Right {Footwear Type: athletic shoe / rigid walking boot / post-op shoe / daily footwear}.
{+ Contralateral Compensation: Matching lift placed on contralateral side to prevent pelvic obliquity and maintain leg length balance.}
{+ Stepped Reduction Plan: Multi-layer wedge system utilized for gradual stepped reduction of heel height per surgical rehabilitation protocol.}

Functional Assessment & Patient Education:
Gait Evaluation: Ambulation evaluated in clinic; patient demonstrated reduced tension at the posterior ankle, improved step length, and a stabilized stance phase without antalgic compensation.

Patient Education: Patient was instructed on proper in-shoe seating, wear schedule {Wear Schedule: during all weight-bearing activities / per post-op orthopedic protocol}, avoidance of barefoot walking, and daily skin checks over the calcaneus. {+ Caregiver Present: Caregiver was present and instructed on proper wedge removal sequencing and footwear safety.}

The shoulder abduction orthosis is reasonable and medically necessary to immobilize the glenohumeral joint in the prescribed plane of abduction, prevent adduction/internal rotation stress on the repaired rotator cuff, offload the shoulder girdle, and promote soft tissue union.

afo-arizona-del.text:
Patient was seen at the North/South office for fitting and delivery of a custom-molded Left/Right Arizona-type Ankle-Foot Orthosis (AFO) custom fabricated from a positive anatomical model of the patient's lower extremity for {Indication: Posterior Tibial Tendon Dysfunction / Severe Subtalar and Talonavicular Osteoarthritis / Chronic Hindfoot Valgus Deformity / Charcot Neuroarthropathy}.

Clinical Justification & Prior Conservative Measures:
Patient exhibits severe medial longitudinal arch collapse, fixed/flexible calcaneal valgus, subtalar hypermobility, and severe midfoot/rearfoot pain that severely limits functional ambulation. Prior conservative therapies (including OTC insoles, prefabricated ankle braces, physical therapy, and NSAIDs) have failed to control joint collapse and pain.

Technical Inspection & Fitting:
The custom AFO was fabricated with a molded thermoplastic shell, total-contact medical grade leather lining, and high medial/lateral longitudinal arch reinforcements. The device was donned and laced securely. Trimlines around the malleoli and navicular were inspected to ensure total surface bearing contact without focal shear. Bony prominences were fully relieved. Subtalar joint was held securely in neutral anatomical alignment. Patient trialed the device in extra-depth footwear across 200 feet of in-office ambulation with marked reduction in pain and elimination of pathological pronation collapse.

Medical Necessity:
The custom molded AFO is reasonable and medically necessary to immobilize and stabilize the subtalar, talocalcaneal, and midtarsal joints in the sagittal, coronal, and transverse planes, offload the degenerated posterior tibial tendon, realign the skeletal structure of the foot/ankle, prevent progressive deformity collapse, and restore ambulatory function.

Patient Instructions:
He/she was provided with verbal and written use/care instructions, taught proper donning/lacing technique, and placed on a strict break-in schedule (increasing wear by 1 hour daily). Instructed to inspect skin daily for redness. Scheduled follow-up in 2-3 weeks.
afo-arizona-del.title: AFO Arizona Delivery

Patient presents with chronic, debilitating unicompartmental joint pain, varus/valgus deformity, and joint space narrowing confirmed on weight-bearing radiographs. Prior conservative treatments (including physical therapy, NSAIDs, intra-articular injections, and unloader sleeves) have failed to provide adequate functional pain relief.

The unloader knee orthosis is reasonable and medically necessary to reduce compressive mechanical loads across the damaged Medial/Lateral knee compartment, stabilize the joint in the coronal plane, decrease arthritic pain, and improve functional ambulatory capacity during daily living activities.

Patient experiences persistent foot drop during the swing phase of gait and muscle fatigue after walking short distances. Current off-the-shelf bracing or lack of bracing provides inadequate energy return and insufficient stability to control dynamic gait deviations. Ambulation is limited to {Ambulation Distance: <100 feet/100-300 feet/300+ feet/community distances} {Assistance: unassisted/with a cane/with a walker} before requiring rest due to fatigue.

Pt. was examined and Left/Right lower extremity assessment revealed dorsiflexion MMT strength of {MMT Dorsiflexion: 0/1/2/2+/3/3+/4/5}. Plantarflexion MMT strength was {MMT Plantarflexion: 0/1/2/2+/3/3+/4/5/WNL}. Knee extensor strength was {MMT Knee Extensors: 3/3+/4/4+/5}. Passive range of motion to neutral (0° dorsiflexion) is {ROM Neutral: achievable with knee extended/achievable with knee flexed/limited}. Severe fixed equinus deformity is {Fixed Deformity: absent/present} and dynamic fluctuating edema is {Edema: absent/present}. Skin integrity is {Skin Integrity: intact/intact with mild erythema/compromised}.

Gait evaluation reveals {Gait Pattern: steppage gait/slap foot at initial contact/knee hyperextension during stance phase/lack of heel-strike} affecting the Left/Right lower extremity during swing and stance phases.

Due to lower extremity weakness and foot drop with high fall risk, patient requires a dynamic carbon fiber AFO (L1951). Standard polypropylene AFOs are inadequate due to the patient's need for dynamic energy storage and return during stance-to-swing transition to reduce fatigue and stabilize gait. Patient meets all Medicare LCD coverage criteria, including ambulatory status, absence of severe fixed deformity or severe edema, and adequate knee/hip strength to manage dynamic propulsion.

Plan: Fit and adjust HCPCS L1951 (carbon fiber dynamic response AFO) to affected Left/Right lower extremity(ies). Custom modifications to include footplate trimming, heel height alignment, and shoe interface fitting. Patient instructed on donning/doffing, skin monitoring, and footwear requirements. Follow-up scheduled in {Follow-up: 2 weeks/4 weeks}.
